name: ORACLE
tagline: Builds a 3-statement financial model and DCF valuation from a company name, with LLM agents for research, comparables and assumption reasoning.
problem: Building a first-pass financial model for a company means gathering comparables, choosing assumptions, and wiring an income statement, cash flow and DCF together by hand. This tool is aimed at analysts who want that scaffold generated quickly, with each calculation step visible and an Excel export that keeps live formulas.
how: The user enters a company name in the ORACLE web UI served by the FastAPI backend.
The orchestrator builds the model progressively: an income statement, then a cash flow statement, then a DCF valuation, recording each calculation step.

Assumptions (starting revenue, growth rates, margins, opex ratios, tax, capex, beta, risk-free rate, terminal growth) drive deterministic calculation modules for revenue, COGS, opex, taxes, capex, working capital, debt and valuation.

In the LLM-backed flows, a questionnaire agent interviews the user, a comparables agent finds peer companies, a research agent gathers web data, and a reasoning agent explains and sanity-checks the assumptions.
Results are shown as statement tables, Chart.js charts and DCF headline figures, and can be exported to an Excel workbook with formulas.
features: Five-step ORACLE flow: company input, research summary, editable assumptions, financial statements, charts and DCF valuation
Income statement with revenue, gross profit, EBITDA and net income over five years
Free cash flow projection and DCF valuation with enterprise value, WACC and terminal value
Agent activity panel that logs each step of the build
Client-side Excel export of the generated model
Alternative autonomous builder and interactive discovery questionnaire pages
React dashboard listing saved models stored in SQLite through a REST API
Settings page to switch between local Ollama models and OpenAI
Industry default benchmarks and Damodaran data loaders for assumptions
ai: QuestionnaireAgent generates interview questions from a company name and classifies the company from the answers.
ComparablesAgent finds and analyses comparable public companies and synthesises assumptions from them.
ResearchAgent performs web research, with Tavily as the optional search provider.
ReasoningAgent analyses a built model step by step and compares it against industry benchmarks.
Agents run on local Ollama models (llama3.1:8b, qwen2.5:7b, mistral:7b) by default or OpenAI (gpt-4o, gpt-4o-mini) when configured.

stack.frontend: Static HTML and JavaScript UI with Chart.js and SheetJS, plus a React 18, Vite and Tailwind dashboard
stack.backend: Python FastAPI with SQLAlchemy and Pydantic settings
stack.data: SQLite by default (PostgreSQL optional), Redis optional for a task queue, file-based research cache
stack.ai: Ollama local LLMs or OpenAI, Tavily web search
stack.deploy: Docker Compose with frontend, backend, Ollama and Redis services

run: cd backend && pip install -r requirements.txt && cp ../.env.example .env && python main.py  (then open http://localhost:8000/static/index.html; React dashboard: cd frontend && npm install && npm run dev)
notes: Ran the FastAPI backend (backend/main.py) with a local SQLite database and the React frontend locally. The ORACLE flow on static/index.html calls /api/orchestrator/quick-model, which builds the statements and DCF deterministically from the default assumptions in the route, so those numbers are real backend output and needed no LLM. The research summary text and the ResearchAgent and ComparablesAgent log lines on that page are fixed strings in the page script, not results of real web searches. The Balance Sheet tab is a placeholder in the code and was not shown. No Ollama, OpenAI or Tavily key was available, so the LLM-driven discovery and questionnaire flows (app.html, app_old.html) were captured only at their input screens. The three dashboard models are the sample models described in LIVE_DEMO.md, created through the real POST /api/models endpoint. Boot changes: Python 3.12 venv without faiss, sentence-transformers and psycopg2; a postcss.config.js was added locally so the existing Tailwind config is applied; the React pages hardcode localhost:8000, so the browser redirected those requests to the backend port; CDN scripts (Chart.js, SheetJS) and Google Fonts were served from local npm copies or fetched through the proxy because the CDN host was blocked.
